쿠팡 Detection Operations 팀은 웹 보안, 네트워크 보안, 이메일 보안, 엔드포인트 보안 전반에 걸쳐보안 Appliance 장비, Endpoint 보안 솔루션, 그리고 다양한 SaaS 기반 보안 서비스를 운영 및 관리하고 있습니다. 우리는 쿠팡의 광범위한 Attack Surface 전반에서 발생하는 사이버 위협을 탐지하고 차단하여 보안 사고로 인한 피해를 최소화하는 동시에, 정확한 원인 분석을 통해 재발 방지 체계를 구축하는 핵심 역할을 수행하고 있습니다. Sr. Manager, Legal Technology Services

San Mateo, CA

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Senior Manager, Legal Technology Services (LTS) will establish and lead a dedicated team within IT Foundational Services (ITFS), part of Digital, Technology and Information, Services (DTIS). The team will support the global Legal, Public Policy & Environment, Social & Governance (LPPESG) organization by providing the technical structure, administration, development, integration and support required to operate the legal technology portfolio reliably and at scale. Reporting to the Vice President of ITFS, with a dotted-line relationship to the Director of Legal Operations, this leader will oversee team development, technical delivery and production services across the portfolio.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Senior Manager will be responsible for standing up the LTS function and lead the phased transition of technology services from Legal Operation to LTS. The leader would balance people leadership, technical delivery and operational accountability across four areas.

Build and Lead Legal Technology Services

• Build, coach and develop a team of legal technology engineers and service professionals responsible for solution delivery and production support.
• Define the function's operating model, service catalog, engagement approach, technical standards and service-management practices.
• Set team objectives and performance expectations, build team capabilities, and align delivery with Legal Operations through the dotted-line relationship to the Director of Legal Operations.
• Foster a culture of customer focus, inclusion, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

Lead Technical Delivery and Platform Lifecycle

• Provide technical leadership across Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM), Document Management System (DMS), Knowledge Management/Search, matter management/Entity Lifecycle Management (ELM), eBilling, Intellectual Property (IP) management, litigation and eDiscovery, legal hold, workflow, compliance, analytics and emerging legal technologies.
• Own the technical lifecycle of legal platforms from architecture and design through configuration, development, integration, deployment, optimization, support and retirement.
• Maintain an integrated view of platform dependencies, lifecycle risk, technical debt and opportunities for standardization or consolidation.
• Translate approved product roadmaps into technical plans, estimates, sequencing and engineering capacity requirements aligned with enterprise standards.
• Lead complex global implementations from solution architecture and system design through deployment, stabilization and transition to support.
• Oversee integrations, data migration, testing, release management and implementation readiness across platforms and geographies.
• Ensure solutions meet enterprise architecture, security, privacy, data governance and technology standards while addressing requirements specific to the Legal organization.

Ensure Secure and Reliable Operations

• Own the technical health, reliability and performance of the legal technology portfolio.
• Establish production support, monitoring, incident and escalation management, problem management, root-cause analysis, release controls and operational service metrics.
• Develop plans for platform resilience, scalability, and recoverability, supported by documentation and knowledge transfer that reduce key-person dependencies.
• Partner with DTIS infrastructure, service management, security, data and engineering teams to ensure legal technology solutions meet enterprise requirements and make effective use of shared capabilities.

Partner, Innovate and Influence

• Build trusted relationships across Legal, Legal Operations, DTIS, Architecture, Information Security, Privacy, Procurement, Finance and other enterprise functions; drive outcomes through influence in a matrixed organization.
• Partner with Legal practice teams as business subject-matter experts and Legal Operations as product owners to translate approved requirements into technology solutions, clearly communicating technical options, dependencies, risks and trade-offs.
• Provide technical evaluation and enablement for approved uses of artificial intelligence, including generative AI, across legal workflows, systems, data and knowledge, ensuring solutions are secure, governed, scalable and maintainable.

Required Experience and Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
• 10+ years of experience in legal technology, enterprise applications, technology consulting or a related field, including significant experience delivering legal technology solutions in complex organizations.
• 5+ years of experience leading technical teams, with direct people-management responsibility and accountability for both solution delivery and production services.
• Demonstrated experience across several areas of the enterprise legal technology landscape.
• Proven success leading large-scale, global technology implementations across architecture, integrations, data migration, testing, deployment and stabilization in a matrixed enterprise.
• Strong understanding of enterprise application architecture, SaaS and cloud technologies, APIs and integrations, identity and access management, data management, information security and service management.
• Strong technical planning, capacity management, stakeholder management and executive communication skills, with the ability to build cross-functional partnerships and influence without direct authority.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

We are looking for a strategic and analytical Revenue Operations Manager to join the Brands team at Roblox. In this role, you will build and own the RevOps function for our Brands advertising business, establishing the rhythm of business, forecasting infrastructure, and GTM operational backbone that enables our Sales and Ad Ops teams to scale. You will be both a systems thinker and a hands-on executor, translating data into executive-ready insights while driving alignment across Sales, Ad Ops, Product, and Finance.

You Will:

Revenue Planning & Forecasting

• Own pipeline and revenue forecasting for the Brands business, maintaining views of funnel health, pacing, and yield across ad products and verticals.
• Build and manage operational dashboards that surface where deals are progressing, stalling, or at risk.
• Define and maintain metric standards (e.g., pipeline stages, pacing benchmarks, utilization rates) to ensure consistent reporting across the team.

Rhythm of Business (RoB)

• Design and run the Brands weekly business review (WBR), including pre-reads, pipeline and pacing commentary, and follow-up tracking.
• Produce executive-ready narratives that translate operational data into clear strategic recommendations.
• Own follow-up tracking and accountability across XFN stakeholders.

GTM & Cross-Functional Execution

• Translate GTM priorities into clear, actionable in-market plans for the Brands Sales and Ad Ops teams.
• Act as the point of contact between Sales, Ad Ops, Product, and Finance to resolve cross-functional misalignment.
• Support quarterly planning processes including territory planning, goaling, and book-building.

Reporting Infrastructure & Automation

• Partner with Data and Engineering to automate manual reporting workflows, moving the team toward real-time dashboards.
• Identify and remove high-friction reporting tasks currently consuming FTE bandwidth.
• Maintain CRM data quality standards to ensure planning and forecasting inputs are accurate and consistent.

Operational Rigor & Process Design

• Document and systematize repeatable operational processes — from media plan intake to campaign pacing to client reporting.
• Identify bottlenecks across the Brands ops workflow and drive resolution in partnership with Product and Engineering.
• Identify opportunities to leverage tooling to reduce manual work and speed up decision-making.

You Have:

• 8+ years of experience in revenue operations, programmatic, sales operations, or a related function within digital advertising or media.
• Strong analytical skills; comfortable building and interpreting pipeline models, pacing dashboards, and funnel analyses. SQL or equivalent data querying experience a plus.
• Experience designing and running a rhythm of business (WBR, QBR, or equivalent) for a sales or revenue-generating team.
• Proven ability to translate complex data into clear executive narratives and drive decisions across senior stakeholders.
• Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; able to drive alignment across Sales, Product, Finance, and Operations.
• Highly organized with a track record of building repeatable, scalable processes.

OpenAI develops models that can reason through complex problems and hardware designed for the demands of advanced AI. AI for Chips connects these efforts: applying increasingly capable AI systems to the work of semiconductor engineering.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Research Engineer to help OpenAI models solve chip-design problems through reinforcement learning, tool use, and evaluation.

You’ll own experiments from the initial idea through implementation and analysis. - Build RL environments and evaluations for tasks such as RTL generation, design verification, and physical design optimization.

- Develop and test approaches that help models use chip-design tools and improve power, performance, and area while preserving correctness.

- Design experiments, establish baselines, and measure whether improvements hold up on new tasks and designs.

- Investigate failures across model behavior, rewards, evaluation tools, and experiment infrastructure.

- Improve iteration speed through better tooling, faster evaluations, and proxy rewards that reflect the outcomes we care about.

- Turn successful experiments into reusable research code and training workflows, working closely with researchers and engineers.

- Have strong programming and debugging skills and a track record of turning technical ideas into working software.

- Experience with reinforcement learning, model evaluations, post-training, or other applied ML research.

- Experience building tool-using agents, reward functions, or automated evaluation systems.

- Can form clear hypotheses, design useful experiments, and distinguish meaningful results from noise or evaluation errors.

- Work independently on ambiguous problems and make practical decisions about what to build or test next.

- Communicate progress clearly and collaborate well with people across research, software, and hardware.

- Care about developing safe, beneficial AI.

NICE TO HAVE:

- Familiarity with experiment orchestration, distributed training, or research infrastructure.

- Experience with RTL, Verilog/SystemVerilog, EDA tools, formal verification, or chip-design automation.

WE ARE GAME MAKERS

Who We Are:

At 31st Union, we are a diverse team of developers driven by a passion for our art, united by our core values and inspired by a culture of inclusivity to build amazing games that thrill players everywhere. We pursue growth and innovation in an environment of safety and trust. Our culture is built on the belief that the more varied voices in our collective will strengthen our team and our games. We are looking for our next teammate who will raise our bar and make us better.

For more information, visit our website at: thirtyfirstunion.com

Who You Are:

We’re looking for a Lead Designer to join our team and help us shape the future of online multiplayer gaming. This role will be a key leader on one of our major gameplay pillars to lead the team on day-to-day work, where you will help the vision come to life, align the team around gameplay objectives and ensure how we design meets a high bar of rigor. You have proven expertise in leading mechanics and systems-based teams and features, developing people and building buy-in through strong working relationships across disciplines to bring things into reality. If you have a passion and drive to bring out the best in others, build teams and shepherd a great experience for players, we’d like to hear from you.

What You’ll Do:

•

Lead a feature team by setting scope, approach and design objectives that meet our overall game goals

•

Manage other designers by giving them support, growth and actionable feedback on both what they work on and how they work

•

Define and set sprint and milestone objectives for your team - including appropriate tradeoffs, costs, and the right areas of work to focus on

•

Evaluate and diagnose work to find improvements and opportunities for improvement - along with plans of how to get there

•

Work cross-functionally within and outside of your team to communicate and align on the work, tradeoffs and dependencies. Radiate changes across the organization

•

Maintain and enforce good executional standards and practices for scripting and design execution - including in-engine and documentation

What Will Make You a Great Fit:

•

8+ years of professional game design experience, including at least 1 year managing, mentoring, and maintaining accountability for multiple designers within a feature team or area on a AAA development team.

•

Background in shaping and building a live-service game or major live-service systems from development through launch.

•

Proven experience designing and leading multiplayer features that touch multiple systems and need strong integration - such as game mode, characters, economy, progression, etc.

•

Theory-crafting skillset & past experience designing for depth and multiplayer gameplay.

•

Deep understanding of the various components (UI, Art, Engineering, Audio, VFX, etc.) to ensure gameplay is cohesive and integrated

•

Proactive approach that creates movement in the right direction

•

Capable of rapidly filtering large volumes of feedback into concrete and useful improvements

•

Adept at managing, articulating and advocating for effective tradeoffs

•

Well-played in the multiplayer PvP / Competitive Space and able to deconstruct what works and why.

•

Capability to abstract designs outside of single solutions into patterns and models of player behavior; providing options and flexible design solutions

•

Strong experience with Unreal Engine and Blueprint visual scripting; programming experience (C++, C#, etc.) is a plus.

The pay range for this position in California at the start of employment is expected to be between $127,500 and $190,000 per year. However, base pay offered is based on market location, and may vary further depending on individualized factors for job candidates, such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other objective business considerations.

Subject to those same considerations, the total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including a bonus and/or equity awards and eligibility to participate in our 401(K) plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program.

Regular, full-time employees are also eligible for a range of benefits at the Company, including: medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance coverage; 14 paid holidays per calendar year; paid vacation time per calendar year (ranging from 15 to 25 days) or eligibility to participate in the Company’s discretionary time off program; up to 10 paid sick days per calendar year; paid parental and compassionate leave; wellbeing programs for mental health and other wellness support; family planning support through Maven; commuter benefits; and reimbursements for fitness-related expenses. jobs.description: The Advanced Safety Specialist provides technical leadership and subject matter expertise for the site's occupational safety and health programs. The position independently manages assigned safety programs, identifies and evaluates workplace hazards, interprets regulatory and company requirements, develops risk-reduction strategies, and partners with site leadership, operations, maintenance, engineering, and employees to drive continuous improvement in safety performance. The role also provides leadership and program management for the site's Emergency Response Team (ERT) and emergency preparedness program. Safety Program Leadership • Independently manage assigned site safety and occupational health programs and ensure compliance with regulatory, corporate, and site requirements. • Serve as a subject matter expert for critical safety programs, which may include Lockout/Tagout, Confined Space Entry, Work Permitting, Respiratory Protection, PPE, Fall Protection, Electrical Safety, Industrial Hygiene, and other life-critical safety systems. • Develop, implement, review, and continuously improve site safety standards, procedures, safe work practices, and supporting documentation. • Evaluate regulatory and company-standard changes and lead implementation of necessary site improvements. • Provide technical guidance to site leadership, supervisors, employees, contractors, engineering, and maintenance personnel. Emergency Preparedness and Response • Serve as the site lead for the Emergency Response Team (ERT) program and provide overall leadership, coordination, and program management for site emergency preparedness and response. • Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the site's emergency response organization, capabilities, and readiness. • Maintain and periodically update the Facility Emergency Preparedness Plan (FEPP) and associated emergency response procedures. • Establish ERT staffing, qualification, training, drill, and competency requirements and ensure the team maintains appropriate readiness to respond to credible site emergencies. • Coordinate and oversee ERT training, drills, exercises, and response evaluations, including development and tracking of corrective actions and lessons learned. • Provide leadership and direction to ERT members and team leaders and ensure clear roles, responsibilities, and expectations are established. • Coordinate emergency preparedness activities with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Occupational Health, Security, Site Leadership, and other applicable functions. • Serve as the primary site liaison with local fire departments, EMS, emergency management agencies, hospitals, and other external emergency-response organizations. • Coordinate periodic joint exercises and planning activities with external response agencies when appropriate. • Evaluate site emergency-response risks, equipment, resources, and capabilities and recommend improvements necessary to maintain effective response readiness. • Manage inspection, testing, maintenance, and readiness requirements for emergency-response equipment and associated resources. • Develop and manage the ERT/emergency preparedness budget and identify resource and capital needs. • Participate in emergency incidents as a member of the site's emergency management structure and provide safety and technical support to incident leadership. • Lead post-drill and post-incident reviews to identify lessons learned and ensure corrective actions are implemented. • Monitor applicable emergency preparedness and response requirements and ensure site programs remain aligned with regulatory, company, and site expectations. Risk Management and Incident Prevention • Lead and participate in workplace hazard assessments, field safety evaluations, audits, inspections, and risk assessments. • Identify systemic safety risks and recommend practical engineering, administrative, and procedural controls. • Participate in Process Safety Reviews, PSSRs, Management of Change activities, project reviews, and other risk-management processes as applicable. • Evaluate work practices and operating conditions to identify opportunities for risk reduction and improved safety performance. • Support development and tracking of corrective actions and verify effective completion. Incident Investigation and Performance Improvement • Lead or participate in investigations of injuries, near misses, safety events, and significant potential incidents. • Apply structured root-cause analysis techniques to identify immediate, contributing, and systemic causes. • Develop and track corrective and preventive actions resulting from investigations. • Analyze safety data and trends to identify emerging risks and recommend targeted improvement initiatives. • Communicate significant findings, trends, and recommendations to site leadership. Regulatory Compliance and Auditing • Interpret applicable OSHA regulations, consensus standards, corporate EHS requirements, and site procedures. • Conduct and support regulatory and internal compliance audits. • Assist with regulatory inspections and development of responses and corrective actions. • Maintain documentation necessary to demonstrate compliance with assigned safety programs. • Stay current on regulatory developments and industry best practices affecting site operations. Industrial Hygiene and Occupational Health • Coordinate and/or conduct occupational exposure assessments, including air and noise monitoring, as appropriate. • Evaluate exposure data and recommend appropriate engineering controls, work practices, PPE, and additional monitoring. • Support administration of the site's respiratory protection program, including fit testing, training, documentation, and equipment selection. • Partner with occupational health resources to address workplace exposure and employee health-protection requirements. Training and Safety Culture • Develop and deliver safety training for employees, contractors, supervisors, and site leadership. • Coach employees and leaders on application of safety requirements and effective risk-management practices. • Promote employee engagement in hazard identification, incident prevention, and continuous improvement. • Serve as a visible field safety resource and build effective working relationships across site functions. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities • Strong working knowledge of OSHA regulations and occupational safety principles. • Knowledge of heavy manufacturing and industrial work environments. • Demonstrated ability to independently manage safety programs and compliance activities. • Strong hazard-recognition and risk-assessment capabilities. • Experience conducting or leading incident investigations and root-cause analyses. • Ability to interpret regulations, technical standards, and corporate requirements and translate them into practical site expectations. • Knowledge of industrial hygiene principles and exposure-assessment practices. • Understanding of life-critical safety programs and controls. • Knowledge of industrial emergency response principles, incident command systems, emergency planning, drills and exercises, and coordination with external response agencies. • Strong written and verbal communication, training, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. • Ability to influence employees and leaders without direct supervisory authority and manage multiple priorities. Education and Experience Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, or a related discipline; or an equivalent combination of education, professional safety training/certification, and relevant experience. Minimum of four (4) years of progressively responsible EHS/Safety experience in a heavy manufacturing, chemical, or industrial environment. Professional safety certifications or advanced safety training such as ASP, CSP, OHST, CHST, OSHA 30-Hour, industrial hygiene training, or equivalent credentials are preferred. Preferred Qualifications • Experience in chemical, polymer, petrochemical, or other high-hazard manufacturing operations. • ASP, CSP, OHST, CHST, CIH, or other recognized EHS certification. • Experience with industrial hygiene monitoring and respiratory protection programs. • Demonstrated experience leading, coordinating, or supporting an Emergency Response Team or emergency preparedness program in an industrial environment. • Emergency response, incident command, HAZWOPER, or EMS training is desirable but is not required as a condition of employment. • Experience participating in regulatory inspections, corporate audits, or management-system audits. • Experience with contractor safety, work permitting, and life-critical safety programs. This Virginia position pays between $90,100 and 148,600/year. Actual pay may vary based on experience, qualifications, and market factors.
